source: Ullman (2023) Large Language Models Fail on Trivial Alterations to Theory-of-Mind Tasks
finding: Takes Kosinski's passed false-belief vignettes and makes small changes that keep ToM logic intact. GPT-3.5 fails them. This is a parsimony test: a cue-following explanation predicts the failures, a belief-tracking one does not.
numbers: Original unexpected-contents: belief prompt P(chocolate)=99% (correct for Sam). Variants where Sam should not think chocolate: transparent bag 95% chocolate; Sam cannot read 98%; trusted friend said popcorn 97%; Sam filled bag and wrote the label herself 87%. Second belief prompt flipped less often (transparent bag: popcorn 58%, chocolate 36%).
quote: a simpler explanation is that LLM reasoning about ToM is sensitive to small irrelevant perturbations
limits: One model (GPT-3.5, completion probabilities), hand-made variants, no human control group. Version 5 corrected an earlier report: a double space in a prompt changed one result, so format sensitivity is itself a finding.
agent_relevance: Template for G3: a pass counts only if it survives a logic-preserving mutated input. Failures outweigh average success.

source: Ullman (2023) same paper, argument section: skeptical zero-hypothesis
finding: Argues the null hypothesis for machine tests should be skeptical, and outlier failures outweigh average success. Rejects Kosinski's dilemma (accept the tests, so LLMs have ToM) because passing a test and using the human algorithm are different claims.
numbers: Multiplication analogy: 100 correct simple products, then failure on 213*261, means no general algorithm, not 99% success.
quote: outlying failure cases should outweigh average success rates
limits: A normative position, not an empirical result.
agent_relevance: Rule for our evaluator: report the worst variant, not the mean over variants.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) Clever Hans or Neural Theory of Mind? Stress Testing Social Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Six ToM tasks, several probing methods, plus adversarial variants (Adv-CSFB). Models show some ToM-like ability but it is not robust. Shortcut learning is the simpler rival explanation.
numbers: ToMi: GPT-3.5 81% overall but 46% on false-belief questions (near random). SocialIQa: GPT-4 79% overall, 61% on the 'others effect' subset. FauxPas-EAI: best model (GPT-4) 27%, below the most-frequent-class baseline. TriangleCOPA: 96% (flan-t5-xxl). Adv-CSFB: GPT-4 97% on original false-belief items but 0% on transparent-access and 'inon' variants.
quote: LLMs struggle with adversarial examples, indicating reliance on shallow heuristics rather than robust ToM abilities
limits: Examples written by one author and verified by another; small adversarial subsets. Probing method shifts accuracy: GPT-4 on SocialIQa differs by 7 points between multiple-choice and CoT probing (400-item sample).
agent_relevance: Newer instruction-tuned models can do worse on adversarial variants than older ones. Re-run mutation tests at every model upgrade.

source: Shapira et al. (2023) - explanations for adversarial failure
finding: Proposes reporting bias and cooperative instruction tuning as reasons: tuned models assume every detail in the prompt matters, so a false label is used even when the protagonist cannot read it.
numbers: Kosinski used 40 examples and Bubeck et al. 10 anecdotes. Decline from davinci-002 to GPT-4: other-person variant 93.8% to 68.8%; inon 71.4% to 0%; transparent access 66.7% to 0%.
quote: LLMs assuming that all details are important, rather than that the input is adversarial
limits: Explanations are hypotheses, not tested by ablation.
agent_relevance: Add a prompt step: which stated facts are irrelevant to the question? Effect untested here.

source: Kosinski (2023/2024) Evaluating large language models in theory of mind tasks
finding: Reports that newer models solve false-belief tasks at child level, with true-belief controls to rule out the 'protagonist is always wrong' strategy. The positive claim that Ullman and Shapira attack.
numbers: 40 false-belief tasks, each with 3 true-belief controls. GPT-3-davinci-002 solved 5%, GPT-3.5-turbo (Mar 2023) 20%, ChatGPT-4 (Jun 2023) 75% (CI95 66-84%), on par with 6-year-olds. Correlation of false-belief and control performance R=0.98.
quote: false-belief tasks can be solved without ToM by simply assuming that the protagonist must be wrong
limits: Same vignettes were later perturbed (c01). Controls are minimal edits, not different-structure tests. Classic tasks may be in training data.
agent_relevance: The pro side of the canon debate: controls were used but were not enough. One factor explaining both scores fits a general text-pattern factor too.

source: Pang et al. (2025) letter responding to Kosinski, invoking Morgan's canon for LLMs
finding: Says isolated ToM task success does not show ToM. Cites Morgan's canon, notes it may lack justification, and lists rival simple explanations: associative learning, explicit training on ToM-like tasks, pattern recognition in human-written data. Proposes a transparent-container test.
numbers: No new numbers. Notes a sudden jump in newer models as a hint of explicit training.
quote: attributing ToM to LLMs may be premature until simpler explanations are ruled out
limits: Short letter without data. The fetch tool's summary of the page did not show mentions of Ullman or Street.
agent_relevance: Turns the canon into an operational list: test association, training exposure and pattern match before crediting reasoning.

source: Hu, Sosa, Ullman (2025) Re-evaluating Theory of Mind evaluation in large language models
finding: Argues disagreement comes from an unclear target: match human behaviour, match the human computation, or match a theory-like generative model. A behavioural pass supports only the first. Uses the lookup-table versus multiplication example.
numbers: No new measurements. Three nested definitions of 'has ToM'.
quote: the model matches people's behavior ... or ... the model uses the same computations that people use
limits: Position paper.
agent_relevance: State the level of each of our claims. Behaviour-level only unless a mutation or process test exists.

source: Systematic review of LLM evaluation on ToM tasks (arXiv 2502.08796)
finding: Review frames the Clever Hans effect (Pfungst 1911) and the stochastic parrot worry as a core dispute: models that solve tasks may rely on memorisation and shallow heuristics. Summarises the Kosinski versus Ullman dilemma.
numbers: Only the introduction and section outline were read; review-level numbers not recorded.
quote: models capable of solving these tasks often rely on memorization and shallow heuristics
limits: Only intro portions inspected.
agent_relevance: Pointer for a later pass: its failure-reason section could seed a shortcut checklist.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Reasoning or Reciting? Counterfactual Tasks
finding: 11 tasks, each with a default and a counterfactual form needing the same procedure (base-9 addition, 1-based indexing, rotated spatial axes, altered guitar tuning). GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Claude and PaLM-2 all drop.
numbers: Counterfactual accuracy above chance but consistently and substantially below default; arithmetic gap sometimes near-perfect to near-zero (paper's words). GPT-3.5 drawing programs parseable: 99% default vs 62%, 71%, 75% for flipped, 90-degree and 180-degree rotation. Better in common bases (8, 16) than in 9, 11. Demonstrations (0 to 16 shots) shrink the addition gap but do not remove it. 0-shot CoT helps most cases but hurts some (PaLM-2 base-10 and 16 addition; chord default tuning).
quote: performance on counterfactual task variants consistently and substantially degrades relative to the performance on the default settings
limits: A counterfactual comprehension check separates misunderstanding from inability; where it is low the conclusion weakens. Closed models of early 2023. Open models were unusable due to poor instruction following.
agent_relevance: Supports G3: test on variants where the surface rule differs but the procedure is the same. CoT can hurt on memorised cases.

source: Wu et al. (2024) - commonness and difficulty analysis
finding: Counterfactual performance tracks how common the counterfactual world is, and default performance predicts counterfactual performance. The authors read this as a memorisation-like effect, the parsimonious rival to abstract reasoning.
numbers: Strong default-counterfactual correlation across difficulty variants (3-4 digit addition, note index, SET with fewer cards shown). Spatial task reverses: GPT-4 best on default but largest counterfactual drop; PaLM-2 worse on default but most robust.
quote: a memorization-like effect where the models perform better under more common conditions
limits: Correlations across variants only; no training-data access.
agent_relevance: Include rare-world variants in probes; a drop that scales with rarity signals recall, not reasoning.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) A Careful Examination of LLM Performance on Grade School Arithmetic (GSM1k)
finding: A freshly written matched set of 1,000 problems compared with GSM8k. Several open model families do worse on the fresh set, consistent with contamination. Frontier models do not.
numbers: Accuracy drops up to 8%. Spearman r^2=0.36 between a model's probability of generating GSM8k items and its GSM8k-GSM1k gap. Phi and Mistral overfit for almost every release and size; Yi, Xwin, Gemma, CodeLlama to a lesser extent; Gemini, GPT, Claude show little or none.
quote: all models broadly demonstrate generalization to novel math problems guaranteed to not be in their training data
limits: Authors say frontier results could be better generalisation or more careful decontamination; cannot tell without training data. r^2 of 0.36 is modest.
agent_relevance: Cleanest contamination test: a fresh matched held-out set. Our G3 held-out check is the same idea at item level.

source: Mirzadeh et al. (2025, ICLR) GSM-Symbolic
finding: Turns GSM8K into templates and samples many instances. Accuracy varies across instances of one question, falls when numbers change, falls more as clauses are added, and drops sharply with an irrelevant but plausible clause (GSM-NoOp).
numbers: Changing names only moves accuracy little; changing numbers drops more; both together drop more again. GSM-NoOp drops up to 65% across models; in the figure o1-preview -17.5, o1-mini -29.1, Mistral-7b-v0.1 -28.3, Gemma2-2b-it -31.8 (accuracy points, 8-shot).
quote: adding seemingly relevant clauses ... significantly drops the performance of all models
limits: The 'not genuine logical reasoning' conclusion is the authors' interpretation of pattern replication. One benchmark family; later models may differ.
agent_relevance: Design for G3: mutate numbers and add a distractor clause; watch the distribution over instances, not a single score.

source: Turpin et al. (2023) Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful CoT
finding: Biasing features (e.g. the answer is always (A) in few-shot examples) change answers but the chain of thought never mentions them. The explanation is a plausible story, not the cause. A parsimony warning against reading the trace as the mechanism.
numbers: Accuracy drops up to 36% on 13 BIG-Bench Hard tasks with GPT-3.5 and Claude 1.0 when biased toward wrong answers. Stereotype-following explanations on BBQ.
quote: CoT explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction
limits: Two 2023 models; limited biasing features.
agent_relevance: Do not treat the stated reasoning as evidence of process. Check outcomes on mutated inputs; use traces as candidate generators (S4 harvest).

source: Sap et al. (2022) Neural Theory-of-Mind? On the Limits of Social Intelligence in Large LMs
finding: Early baseline: GPT-3 lacks ToM on SocialIQa and ToMi.
numbers: Few-shot GPT-3 reaches 55% and 60% on the two tasks, well below human accuracy.
limits: 2022 model; later models score higher (c05, c15).
agent_relevance: Baseline that makes later jumps look sudden; a jump hard to explain by scale supports the training-exposure rival.

source: Street et al. (2024) LLMs achieve adult human performance on higher-order ToM
finding: New handwritten Multi-Order ToM Q&A suite (reducing training exposure) and a new adult benchmark. GPT-4 and Flan-PaLM at or near adult level; GPT-4 above adults at 6th order.
numbers: True/false statements, N=112 per model/order. GPT-4: order 3 94.6%, order 4 73.2%, order 6 92.9%. Flan-PaLM: order 3 94.6%, order 4 78.6%, order 5 76.8%, order 6 71.4%. Humans: order 3 92.9%, order 4 82.1%, order 5 98.2%.
quote: the best-performing LLMs have developed a generalised capacity for ToM
limits: Chance is 50%; GPT-4 better at order 6 than 4 is odd and may reflect statement-form artefacts; no perturbation test.
agent_relevance: Positive evidence with newly written items; a way to build contamination-resistant probes. Still behaviour-level only (c07).

source: Gandhi et al. (2023) Understanding Social Reasoning in LMs with LMs (BigToM)
finding: Procedurally generated benchmark from causal templates (25 controls, 5,000 model-written evaluations), rated by humans as high quality as expert-written. GPT-4 mirrors human inference patterns but less reliably; other LLMs struggle.
numbers: 5,000 items plus 25 controls. Per-model table cells not extracted.
quote: GPT4 has ToM capabilities that mirror human inference patterns, though less reliable, while other LLMs struggle
limits: Model-written evaluations; only abstract and a few table lines read.
agent_relevance: Procedural generation yields unlimited fresh items, the tool for a rolling contamination-proof G3 check.

source: Kim et al. (2023) FANToM: stress-testing machine ToM in conversations
finding: Asks several question types that need the same underlying reasoning; consistency across them is the test for illusory ToM. Models pass single questions but fail the set.
numbers: Short-conversation table, zero-shot CoT, first column (belief-style metric, as read from the table): human 87.5; GPT-4 0613 26.6 (Jun) and 14.8 (Oct); ChatGPT 0613 3.7; Llama-2 Chat 0.4; Mistral Instruct 0.1; fine-tuned Flan-T5 XL 53.7.
quote: formulate multiple types of questions that demand the same underlying reasoning to identify illusory or false sense of ToM capabilities
limits: Column header was not cleanly extracted from the PDF text, so which metric the first column is should be checked against the paper. GPT-4 scores differ between June and October snapshots (model drift).
agent_relevance: Consistency across related questions is a cheap parsimony filter: a shortcut rarely survives six probes of one fact.

source: McCoy, Pavlick, Linzen (2019) Right for the Wrong Reasons: HANS
finding: Older Clever Hans work in NLP: NLI models trained on MNLI, including BERT, score high but follow lexical-overlap, subsequence and constituent heuristics. On HANS items where the heuristics fail, they score near zero.
numbers: All four models nearly always predicted entailment: near-perfect on entailment items, near-zero on non-entailment items, below chance overall. Appendix G has exact values. Adding HANS-like training data hurt DA and SPINN on MNLI (66.0 vs 72.4, 63.9 vs 67.0) but not BERT or ESIM.
quote: All models behaved as we would expect them to if they had adopted the heuristics targeted by HANS
limits: Pre-LLM models. Later large LMs were not tested here.
agent_relevance: Write the suspected shortcut down first, then build items where it fails.

source: Binz and Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: Runs canonical decision, information search, deliberation and causal tasks on GPT-3. Often human-like or better on standard vignettes, but small perturbations send it astray and it fails causal reasoning.
numbers: Outperforms humans in a multi-armed bandit; no signatures of directed exploration; fails a blicket-type causal task. Exact percentages not extracted.
quote: small perturbations to vignette-based tasks can lead GPT-3 vastly astray
limits: GPT-3 era; famous tasks probably in training data.
agent_relevance: Same pattern as c01: famous tasks pass, perturbed ones fail. Use novel variants of classic tasks.

source: Golchin and Surdeanu (2024) Time Travel in LLMs: Tracing Data Contamination
finding: Prompt the model with dataset name, partition and the first segment of an item; flag contamination if it completes the rest, compared with a generic prompt.
numbers: Best method 92-100% accurate against human labels across seven datasets (14 partitions) for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4. Algorithm 1 BLEURT 11/14 (GPT-4) vs 9/14 (GPT-3.5); ROUGE-L 13/14 vs 7/14; Algorithm 2 GPT-4 ICL 14/14 vs 13/14.
limits: Needs the model to reproduce memorised text; instruction tuning can hide it. Ground truth built by deliberately contaminating partitions.
agent_relevance: Usable pre-flight check: if a model completes test items from a name and a prefix, treat its score as suspect.

source: Oren et al. (2024) Proving test set contamination in black box LMs
finding: If a model is uncontaminated, every ordering of an exchangeable benchmark is equally likely. If canonical order is much likelier than shuffled order, flag it. Gives false-positive control.
numbers: Detects test sets of 1,000 examples in a 1.4B model, sometimes with only 2 duplicates; vanishing p-values at 10 or more duplicates. Audit of four public models: mostly non-significant; AI2-ARC on Mistral p=0.001, borderline after multiple-testing correction.
quote: Failure to reject the null hypothesis is not direct evidence in favor of the null
limits: Needs log-probabilities, so not usable on closed chat APIs; exchangeable test sets only.
agent_relevance: Useful for open models; for closed APIs use fresh sets (c11) and mutations (c12).

source: Cross-paper synthesis: scaffolds and prompts do not close the gap (c03, c09, c13, c17)
finding: No scaffold removed the gap between default and perturbed performance. CoT helps on many counterfactual cases and hurts on some default ones; demonstrations narrow but do not close the gap; probe format moves results by several points.
numbers: Wu: 0 to 16 shots reduce but do not remove the base-9 addition gap. Shapira: 7-point MC vs CoT gap for GPT-4 on SocialIQa. Turpin: CoT does not prevent bias (drops up to 36%). FANToM: CoT GPT-4 about 27 vs human 87.5 on the first table column.
limits: Different tasks and models; the synthesis is mine.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a thinking scaffold fixes shortcut use; measure mutated-input accuracy per scaffold.

source: Design pattern across studies: logic-preserving mutation plus controls
finding: Four groups use one recipe: keep the logic, change surface features, compare. Ullman changes perceptual access; Wu changes world rules; Mirzadeh changes numbers and adds a no-op clause; Kim asks many questions about one fact.
limits: Different domains; none of the papers read is a meta-analysis.
agent_relevance: Define pass in G3 as: right on the original, right on a logic-preserving mutation, not distracted by a no-op clause.

source: Kosinski (2024) true-belief controls as a parsimony control
finding: Author notes false-belief tasks may be solved by assuming the protagonist is wrong, so he adds true-belief controls. A model that guesses false belief everywhere fails them. Ullman later extends this with perceptual and testimony variants.
numbers: 3 true-belief controls per task, 40 tasks; ChatGPT-4 solves 75% of tasks (CI95 66-84%).
quote: if a respondent maintains that a protagonist should hold false-beliefs in a true-belief scenario, it suggests that they are guessing
limits: Controls rule out one strategy (always wrong), not label-word association.
agent_relevance: A control is only as good as the shortcut it targets. List shortcuts first (c18).

source: Gap: Morgan's canon inside LLM agent loops
finding: I found no paper that puts Morgan's canon or an explicit simpler-explanation rule inside an LLM agent loop. Closest practices: consistency across related questions (c17), invariance under mutation (c12), contamination audits (c20, c21). Search quota was used up and API search was rate limited, so this is an absence in my reading, not proof.
numbers: 0 agent-loop implementations found.
limits: Search coverage poor; nothing opened for this line.
agent_relevance: Open idea: add 'name the simplest rival explanation and a test that separates it' to the verify state.

source: Comparative-psychology works (Heyes, Shettleworth, Buckner) not opened
finding: The key works named in the subfield table were not opened by this angle. No numbers recorded. Flagged so nobody counts it as evidence.
numbers: none
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Belongs to the founding-studies angles.
